overview: This Senate resolution honors the service members and families involved in Operation Midnight Hammer, the June 21, 2025, U.S. military strike on nuclear facilities in Iran. According to the resolution, seven B-2 stealth bombers flying from Whiteman Air Force Base in Missouri dropped 14 large bunker-busting bombs on the Fordow and Natanz uranium enrichment sites, while a Navy submarine fired Tomahawk cruise missiles at targets near Isfahan. It commends the pilots, maintainers, analysts, sailors and others for their skill and dedication, calls the mission the largest B-2 combat strike in U.S. history, and recognizes the sacrifices of their families. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on October 6, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution rightly honors the skill and courage of the crews and support personnel who carried out a long and complex mission, and the families who supported them.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and changes no law, and that its preamble presents the extent of damage to Iran's nuclear program as settled even though the resolution itself notes Iran disputes it.
